correctness.rationale: Exact explicit graph on 11 vertices, 18 edges. Two independent exhaustive methods enumerate 751 nonempty matching simplices. A concrete deterministic staged toggle matching has 369 pairs and critical cells only in dimensions 0 (one) and 3 (twelve); a full DAG check of all 2,502 covering relations proves acyclicity. Forman discrete Morse yields a CW model with one point and twelve 3-cells, proving the integral wedge type. The group S3 x C2 is established by unique degree/neighborhood labels, all 12 Lefschetz characters are reproduced by two exact methods, and irreducible multiplicities are integer character inner products. Simplicial boundary ranks (17,94,186,72) over 2,3,5,101 corroborate the result without masquerading as an integral certificate.

The closest indexed named-graph comparison is Goldner–Harary, a different graph, and the indexed Herschel independence complex differs from the line-graph independence complex. value.rationale: The Herschel graph is the canonical smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph. Computing its exact integral matching-complex homotopy type gives a naturally motivated complete finite classification. The complete S3 x C2 rational character, including a one-dimensional invariant subspace and a 5/7 central eigenspace split, provides genuine symmetry data not implied by Euler characteristic or Betti ranks. This offers a specific nonouterplanar planar benchmark and a contrast with a different eleven-vertex nonhamiltonian polyhedral graph. No general planar-graph claim is implied.
